label: Reasoning over the whole society (Nemotron Ultra)

headline: Zomato's ₹2 platform fee will be grudgingly accepted — users complain loudly but 45% still order, because switching costs and habit outweigh a two-rupee irritant.
say_do_gap: People say they oppose it (63% oppose, only 15% support) but 45% still intend to adopt — the ₹2 fee is below the pain threshold that triggers actual switching.
summary: Opposition hardens early (net -0.50) and stays flat; support halves from 25% to 15%. Yet adoption intent settles at 45% because the fee is too small to overcome Zomato's speed and habit advantage. Lower-income users (₹15–35k, net -0.85) threaten to leave but lack viable alternatives; Gold members feel devalued but stay locked in.

drivers.explanation: 35% 'Convenience Over Cost' theme + 20% 'Habitual Dependence' = 55% of users cite speed/habit as reason to stay; adoption 45% vs support 15% proves behavior sticks.
30% 'Frustration Over Nickel-and-Diming' theme concentrated in ₹15–35k (net -0.85, adopt 32%) and <₹15k (net -0.77, adopt 35%) — the loudest opponents, lowest adoption.
10% 'Gold Membership Devaluation' theme; Gold users charged same fee, destroying loyalty signal — sample shows Gold holders calling it 'waste' yet still ordering.
₹75k–2L segment near-neutral (net -0.06, adopt 59%); >₹2L adopt 61% despite net -0.33 — high earners dismiss ₹2 as trivial (5% 'Minor Irritation' theme).

segments_at_risk.why: Net -0.85, only 32% adoption intent — most price-sensitive working class, feel squeezed by cumulative fees, actively comparing Swiggy.
Net -0.77, 35% adoption — students and gig workers for whom ₹2/order compounds; quote: 'already paise kamane ke liye pareshan hoon'.
Net -0.57, lowest adoption 35% — older users less habit-locked, more fee-aware, no Gold buffer.

surprise: Women oppose more strongly (net -0.55 vs -0.45) but adopt more (49% vs 42%) — they complain louder but switch less, likely due to household ordering responsibility and higher switching friction.
fix: Exempt Zomato Gold members from the ₹2 platform fee — this single change neutralizes the 10% Gold-devaluation theme, rewards the highest-LTV users, and gives a clear 'join Gold to avoid fees' upsell lever without reducing revenue from non-Gold orders.
rewrite: Zomato introduces a ₹2 platform fee on every food-delivery order, waived for Zomato Gold members. The fee applies on top of delivery charges and taxes. Gold membership (₹XXX/year) now includes unlimited platform-fee-free orders, reinforcing the loyalty tier while monetizing non-members.
watch_outs: Swiggy matching the fee within 60 days — duopoly pricing parity will erase Zomato's convenience edge and force real churn.
Regulatory scrutiny on 'platform fee' labeling — if classified as hidden charge, could trigger consumer-protection action.
Gold membership cannibalization — if too many upgrade just to avoid ₹2, average revenue per user may drop unless Gold price rises.
Cumulative fee fatigue — next ₹2 add-on (packaging, rain surcharge) could push ₹15–35k segment past breaking point (current adopt 32%).

backtest.actual_text: Users complained on social media but kept ordering. Zomato raised the fee about six times in a year, reaching ₹10 per order in October 2024, and Swiggy followed with a similar fee.
